mainTopic: Where סתם חרמים go, how each side learns its laws, רב's ruling, the פומבדיתא case, and רבי ישמעאל on consecrating a בכור
overview: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. חרמי כהנים cannot be redeemed: they are הקדש while still with the owner and become ordinary חולין once the כהן receives them. It then asks what each side of the משנה's מחלוקת learns from the other side's פסוק. רבי יהודה בן בתירא uses ״כשדה החרם״ to teach that a כהן who made his own שדה חרם into הקדש does not keep it at the יובל. The רבנן learn that law from the extra ה in ״החרם״. Next, רב rules like רבי יהודה בן בתירא, and the גמרא explains this through a tradition that reverses the names in the משנה. A story in פומבדיתא shows רב יהודה letting a man redeem his חרם onto four זוזים, while עולא would have given everything to the כהנים. A ברייתא ties שדה החרם to the יובל, and the גמרא answers that this applies only to land in ארץ ישראל. Finally, a new משנה has רבי ישמעאל settle two clashing פסוקים about making a בכור holy, the גמרא explains the רבנן's reading, and the chapter ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: Priestly dedications cannot be redeemed and go to the priest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חרמי כהנים have no פדיון and must be given to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins. The Sages taught: property dedicated for the priests cannot be redeemed, and it is given to the priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that states the basic rule of חרמי כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With regular הקדש, the owner can usually pay money to redeem the item. With חרמי כהנים there is no such option: the item itself must go to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated (declared חרם) for the priests
Redemption: buying back a holy item with money
The discussion of the Talmud that follows the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara
The Sages taught:
Dedications for priests have no redemption
and they are given to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים אֵין לָהֶן פִּדְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חרמי כהנים cannot be redeemed and must be given to a כהן.

steps.title: Holy while with the owner, ordinary once with the priest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: חרמים are like הקדש while still with the owner, and like חולין once given to the כהן. Each half has its own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as the dedicated items are still in the owner's house, they are treated like consecrated property in every way. The verse says: 'Every dedicated item in Israel is most holy to ה׳.' Once he gives them to the priest, they are like ordinary property in every way. The verse says: 'Every dedicated item in Israel shall be yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains that a חרם has two stages. Holy while still with the owner, ordinary once the כהן receives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the item is handed over, it carries the status of הקדש, so using it would be like using holy property. Once the כהן receives it, it becomes his private property, fully חולין. Each stage is backed by its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property belonging to the Temple
Ordinary, non-holy property
Still in the owner's possession
Most holy

steps.whatToRemember: A חרם is holy until it reaches the כהן. After that it is simply the כהן's own property.
steps.confusionAlert: The same חרם does not stay holy forever. Its status changes the moment the כהן receives it.

phrases.aramaic: חֲרָמִים כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהֵן בְּבֵית בְּעָלִים
phrases.english: Dedications, as long as they are in the owner's house,
are like consecrated property in every respect,
as it is said: 'Every dedicated item in Israel
is most holy to ה׳.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28

phrases.english: Once he gave them to the priest,
they are in every respect like ordinary property,
as it is said: 'Every dedicated item in Israel shall be yours.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:14. 'Yours' means the כהן's own private property.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲרָמִים כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהֵן בְּבֵית בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the two stages of a חרם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before reaching the כהן a חרם is הקדש. After reaching him it is חולין.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה בן בתירא learn from 'as a dedicated field'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא. The רבנן explain both their own פסוק and his. The גמרא asks what he does with the רבנן's פסוק ״כשדה החרם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says unspecified dedications go to Temple upkeep, etc. Granted, the רבנן explain their own reason and also the reason of רבי יהודה בן בתירא. But what does רבי יהודה בן בתירא do with this verse, 'as a dedicated field'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's מחלוקת and asks a question. The רבנן's פסוק must teach something, so what does רבי יהודה בן בתירא learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן use ״כשדה החרם... לכהן״ to show that סתם חרמים go to the כהנים. They also reinterpret רבי יהודה בן בתירא's פסוק. But he never explained what the רבנן's פסוק is for, and a פסוק cannot be left with no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedications made without saying who they are for
The fund for Temple maintenance
'Granted…': accepting one side before raising a question on the other
'What does he do with it?': what does he learn from this פסוק?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
Unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance, etc.
Granted, the Rabbis
are fine, as they explain their own reason
and the reason of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
but Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
this verse 'as a dedicated field,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to the משנה's מחלוקת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה בן בתירא learns from ״כשדה החרם״, since he does not use it to say that סתם חרמים go to כהנים

steps.title: He needs the verse for a priest who consecrated his own dedicated field
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי יהודה בן בתירא needs the פסוק for a ברייתא about a כהן who made his שדה חרם into הקדש. Without the פסוק, the כהן might claim it stays his at the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'As a dedicated field, its possession shall be the priest's.' Why does the verse say this? To teach about a priest who consecrated his dedicated field. He may not say: 'Since such a field goes out to the priests, and it is already in my hands, it should be mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה בן בתירא uses the פסוק for a different law, taught in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a field that was made הקדש and not redeemed goes to the כהנים at the יובל. Here the owner is himself a כהן who received the field as a חרם. He might argue that since it goes to כהנים anyway, he can just keep it. The פסוק is needed to block that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for (a different teaching)
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
A field he received as a חרם
Ancestral land holding

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that both sides of the מחלוקת use every פסוק. The disagreement is only about which law each פסוק teaches.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught:
'As a dedicated field, its possession shall be the priest's,'
why does the verse need to say this?
From where do we know, about a priest who consecrated his dedicated field,
that he may not say:
'Since it goes out to the priests,'
phrases.notes: He means at the יובל, when an unredeemed הקדש field passes to the כהנים.

phrases.english: and it is already in my hands,
it should be mine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה בן בתירא uses ״כשדה החרם״ to teach that a כהן who made his שדה חרם into הקדש does not keep it at the יובל.

steps.title: A logical argument that the priest should keep it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא spells out the כהן's argument as a קל וחומר: if he gains other people's fields, surely he should gain his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical: if I acquire fields belonging to others, shouldn't I all the more so acquire my own?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows why the פסוק is needed: without it, a strong קל וחומר would give the field to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the יובל, a כהן receives unredeemed הקדש fields that belonged to other people. So it seems obvious that a field which was already his should stay with him. This argument sets up the פסוק that will reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is logical': introduces a reasoning that the פסוק will override
All the more so: the conclusion of a קל וחומר
Acquires, gains ownership

phrases.english: And it is logical:
if I acquire what belongs to others,
then my own, all the more so, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the כהן's claim in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the כהן loses his own consecrated field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if a כהן gains strangers' fields at the יובל, he should surely keep his own.

steps.title: The verse overrides the logic
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחזתו״ teaches that the כהן does not keep the field, despite the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the verse says: 'As a dedicated field, its possession shall be the priest's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא concludes that the פסוק is needed to reject the כהן's logical claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since logic would have given the field to the כהן, the פסוק is not saying something obvious. It teaches a new law: the field is treated like any חרם and goes to the כהנים in general, not back to this כהן. That gives רבי יהודה בן בתירא a full use for the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Therefore the פסוק says': the פסוק teaches against the logical argument

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בן בתירא uses ״כשדה החרם״ to teach that a כהן who made his own שדה חרם into הקדש does not get it back at the יובל. That is why he does not need it for סתם חרמים.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says:
'As a dedicated field, its possession shall be the priest's.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21. The field goes to the כהנים as a group, not back to this כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 5 using the פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק overrides the קל וחומר: a כהן does not keep his own consecrated שדה חרם. This is the law רבי יהודה בן בתירא learns from ״כשדה החרם״.

steps.title: The verse compares the כהן's field to a ישראל's ancestral field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that the פסוק never actually told us the law of a שדה חרם. So the שדה חרם, which was supposed to teach, is really the one being taught. The פסוק links it to a ישראל's שדה אחוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what did we really learn from 'a dedicated field'? Nothing new, since we never knew its law. So this case came to teach but ends up being taught: the verse compares the כהן's dedicated field to a ישראל's ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the פסוק teaches the law from Step 6. It shows that the comparison actually works backwards from what we expected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the field becomes the כהן's 'like a שדה חרם,' which sounds like we are learning from the שדה חרם. But the Torah never told us what happens to a כהן's own שדה חרם that he made הקדש. So really the שדה חרם is the one learning, from the ישראל's שדה אחוזה it is compared to.

keyTerms.meaning: A case that 'comes to teach' but ends up being the one taught
Compares or links two cases so that they share the same law (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
The field a כהן received as חרם, which is now his
An ancestral field that a family inherited

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the שדה חרם is the source of the law here. The ברייתא's whole point is the opposite: the שדה חרם gets its law from the ישראל's שדה אחוזה.

phrases.english: But what have we learned
from a dedicated field, then?
phrases.notes: The פסוק says 'like a שדה חרם,' but we were never told what happens to that kind of field, so the comparison teaches us nothing yet.

phrases.english: This comes to teach
and is found to be taught:
it compares his dedicated field
to the ancestral field of a Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה לָמַדְנוּ מִשְּׂדֵה חֵרֶם מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from Step 6 actually produces its lesson
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק links a כהן's שדה חרם to a ישראל's שדה אחוזה; the שדה חרם is the case being taught.

steps.title: Both fields leave the owner and are divided among the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is spelled out. A ישראל's שדה אחוזה leaves his hands and is divided among the כהנים. In the same way, the כהן's שדה חרם leaves his hands and is divided among his fellow כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as a ישראל's ancestral field leaves his possession and is divided among the כהנים, so too the כהן's dedicated field leaves his possession and is divided among his brothers, the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out exactly what the comparison teaches. The כהן does not keep his own field. It goes to all his fellow כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the כהן's קל וחומר from Step 5. He argued that he should surely keep his own field. The הקש says no: his field is treated like anyone else's, so it is shared among the כהנים and not kept by him alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaves his possession
Is divided among the כהנים
His brothers, the other כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who makes his own שדה חרם into הקדש does not get it back. Like a ישראל's שדה אחוזה, it is divided among all the כהנים.

phrases.english: Just as the ancestral field of a Yisrael
leaves his possession
and is divided among the priests,
so too his dedicated field
leaves his possession
and is divided among his brothers, the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the הקש from Step 7 to give the final law
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן's own שדה חרם leaves him and is divided among the כהנים, just like a ישראל's שדה אחוזה.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן learn this law?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן already use ״כשדה החרם״ to teach that a plain חרם goes to the כהנים. So the גמרא asks where they learn the law about the כהן's own field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side, the רבנן: where do they learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks for their source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירא uses the פסוק for the כהן's field. But the רבנן need that same פסוק for their own view, that a plain חרם goes to the כהנים. So it seems they have no source left for this law.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: the other opinion in the מחלוקת

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: 'The other' is the רבנן. They used ״כשדה החרם״ for their own view, so where do they get the law about the כהן's field?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי יהודה בן בתירא's use of the פסוק is explained, asks how the רבנן cover the same law
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's source for the law that a כהן's consecrated שדה חרם leaves him

steps.title: The רבנן learn it from the extra letter ה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said just ״חרם״, but it says ״החרם״. The רבנן learn a second lesson from that extra ה, so one פסוק gives them both laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from the difference between 'חרם' and 'החרם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן find an extra hint in the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״חרם״ alone would teach the רבנן's main point, that a plain חרם goes to the כהנים. The added ה in ״החרם״ is extra, so they use it for the second law, about the כהן's own field.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Dedicated' and 'the dedicated': the extra ה gives a second lesson

phrases.english: From 'חרם' to 'החרם'.
phrases.notes: The פסוק could have said 'חרם' but says 'החרם' with an extra ה, so the רבנן learn one more law from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn both laws from one פסוק: one from ״חרם״ and one from the extra ה of ״החרם״.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not learn from the extra ה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not do the same thing. He does not learn anything from the difference between ״חרם״ and ״החרם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other, רבי יהודה בן בתירא, does not learn anything from 'חרם' versus 'החרם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה בן בתירא gets only one law from this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה בן בתירא the ה is not extra, so ״כשדה החרם״ teaches him only the law of the כהן's own field. His own view on plain חרמים comes from ״כל חרם... קדש קדשים״, so he does not need this פסוק for it.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not mean anything to him; he does not learn from it

phrases.english: And the other: 'חרם', 'החרם'
phrases.notes: Here 'the other' is רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

phrases.english: does not teach him anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not use the ה the way the רבנן did in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not learn anything from the extra ה in ״החרם״.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה בן בתירא learn that חרם takes effect on קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn that חרם takes effect on קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים from a פסוק that רבי יהודה בן בתירא uses for his own view. So the גמרא asks what his source is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה בן בתירא: where does he learn that a חרם takes effect on קדשי קדשים and on קדשים קלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה בן בתירא's source for a different law. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side used its פסוקים for its own views. Since רבי יהודה בן בתירא used the פסוק that the רבנן learn this law from for his own opinion, he seems to be missing a source for this law.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes effect
Offerings of the most sacred level
Offerings of lesser holiness
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira:
that it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred level
and on offerings of lesser holiness,
from where does he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא, דְּחָל עַל קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וְעַל קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the field law to another law that needs a source in רבי יהודה בן בתירא's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה בן בתירא's source that חרם takes effect on קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים

steps.title: He follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא agrees with רבי ישמעאל, who learns this law from a different source.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה בן בתירא gets this law the same way רבי ישמעאל does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learn this law from ״כל חרם... קדש קדשים״, but רבי יהודה בן בתירא already uses that פסוק for plain חרמים. So he takes this law from רבי ישמעאל's source instead. רבי ישמעאל's reading appears in the משנה in steps 40–41.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (the view of) someone else

steps.whatToRemember: Every view needs a source for each law. The רבנן get two laws from ״חרם״ and ״החרם״. רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not learn from the extra ה, and for חרם on קדשים he relies on רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה בן בתירא follows רבי ישמעאל's source for the law that חרם takes effect on קדשים.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יהודה בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: רב says the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The law is like רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a ruling on the מחלוקת in our משנה. He says we follow רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהודה בן בתירא says plain חרמים go to בדק הבית, and the חכמים say they go to the כהנים. רב sides with the single Sage, and the next steps will question that.

keyTerms.meaning: The binding law, the view we actually follow

phrases.english: Rav said:
The law is like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources for each side to a ruling on which side we follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא that plain חרמים go to בדק הבית.

steps.title: Would רב leave the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: why follow one Sage against the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: Would רב really leave the רבנן and act like רבי יהודה בן בתירא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised at רב's ruling. Normally we follow the majority, not one Sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that when one Sage argues with the רבנן, the הלכה follows the רבנן. רב seems to break that rule, so the גמרא demands an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaves aside, abandons
Acts, rules in practice
The majority of the Sages

phrases.english: And would Rav leave aside the Rabbis
and act like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שָׁבֵיק רַבָּנַן וְעָבֵיד כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling like the single Sage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה normally follows the majority, not one Sage against them.

steps.title: The ברייתא has the names reversed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא switches the names, so רבי יהודה בן בתירא's ruling there is the רבנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches it the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a ברייתא tells the מחלוקת with the names switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the רבנן are the ones who say plain חרמים go to בדק הבית. So רב's ruling actually matches the majority there.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
The opposite way, reversed

phrases.english: A baraita is taught the opposite way,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source that reverses the names
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב follows one Sage against the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the ברייתא, רב's ruling is the majority view.

steps.title: Would רב leave the משנה for a ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why would רב follow a ברייתא over our משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Would he leave the משנה and act like the ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. A משנה usually carries more weight than a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the ברייתא gives the ruling to the רבנן, our משנה gives it to the single Sage. Normally we rely on the משנה, so the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה

phrases.english: Would he leave aside the mishna and act like the baraita?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה outweighs a ברייתא, so רב should follow the משנה's version.

steps.title: רב reverses the משנה too
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the משנה with the names switched as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב also teaches the משנה the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב does not go against the משנה. In his version of the משנה, the names are switched too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה and ברייתא agree in רב's version: the רבנן say plain חרמים go to בדק הבית. So רב follows both the משנה and the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, as well

phrases.english: Rav teaches the mishna also the opposite way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה so it matches the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: In רב's version, the משנה is also reversed.

steps.title: Why change the משנה and not the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה should be adjusted to fit the ברייתא, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you reverse the משנה because of the ברייתא? Reverse the ברייתא because of the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice. If the two sources clash, it would make more sense to fix the ברייתא to match the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is the main text, so it should be the anchor. Switching the משנה to fit a ברייתא seems backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why did you choose this way?
Because of, in the face of
Let us reverse

phrases.english: What did you see that you reversed the mishna
because of the baraita?
Let us reverse the baraita because of the mishna!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חֲזֵית דְּאָפְכַתְּ מַתְנִיתִין מִקַּמֵּי בָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה is the stronger source, so the ברייתא should be adjusted instead.

steps.title: רב had a tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב learned from his teachers that the משנה should be reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב learned it as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב did not decide this on his own. He received it from his teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a guess based on the ברייתא. רב had a tradition that the names in this משנה are switched.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned it as a received tradition

phrases.english: Rav learned it as a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב reversed the משנה only to fit the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב had a tradition from his teachers to reverse the משנה.

steps.title: Then רב should have said 'like the רבנן'
steps.stepSummary: If רב switches the names, his ruling is the רבנן's view, so why does he name רבי יהודה בן בתירא?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why say 'like רבי יהודה בן בתירא'? He should have said 'like the רבנן'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a new problem in רב's wording. In his own version, the view he follows belongs to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched, 'plain חרמים go to בדק הבית' is the רבנן's view. So it is odd that רב credits it to רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
He should have said

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא?
phrases.english: If so, why 'like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira'?
He should have said 'like the Rabbis'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא? כְּרַבָּנַן מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 20 to attack the wording of step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב's own version the view belongs to the רבנן, so naming רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not fit.

steps.title: רב was speaking to the listeners' version
steps.stepSummary: רב meant: in the version you learned, that view is called רבי יהודה בן בתירא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: According to the way you reversed and taught it, the law is like רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's wording. He used the names as his listeners knew them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His students had the משנה in the common version, where the בדק הבית view is under רבי יהודה בן בתירא. רב named the view the way they would recognize it, without changing his own reading.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
According to the way you switched it

steps.whatToRemember: רב's tradition switches the names in the משנה. Either way, the הלכה is that plain חרמים go to בדק הבית.
steps.confusionAlert: From רב's point of view, 'the way you reversed it' is the common version of the משנה. He sees the common version as the switched one.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
According to the way you reversed it and taught it,
the law is like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 and closes the discussion of רב's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording as spoken to the listeners' version
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's wording contradicts his own reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב named the view the way it appears in his students' version.

steps.title: A man in פומבדיתא declares his property חרם
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells a man to redeem his חרם property onto four זוזים and throw them in the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man in פומבדיתא declared his property חרם. He came before רב יהודה. רב יהודה told him: Take four זוזים, transfer the holiness onto them, throw them into the river, and the property will be permitted to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case. רב יהודה shows the man how to get his property back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the holiness onto coins makes the property ordinary again. The coins now hold the holiness and may not be used, so he throws them away in the river.

keyTerms.meaning: He declared them חרם
Silver coins
Transfer the holiness, redeem
They will become permitted

phrases.english: A certain man declared his property חרם in Pumbedita,

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: he came before Rav Yehuda, who said to him:
Take four zuz and transfer the holiness onto them,
and throw them into the river,
and they will be permitted to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical case connected to the same מחלוקת about plain חרמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה allows redeeming plain חרם property onto four זוזים.

steps.title: So רב יהודה holds plain חרמים go to בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: From the story, the גמרא infers that רב יהודה holds plain חרמים go to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see he holds: plain חרמים go to בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from רב יהודה's advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חרם that belongs to the כהנים cannot be redeemed. Since רב יהודה let the man redeem it, he must hold that a plain חרם goes to בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see, it follows
He holds
חרמים declared without saying who they are for
The fund for upkeep of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: So we see he holds:
plain חרמים go to the Temple upkeep fund.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר: סְתַם חֲרָמִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal point out of the story in step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה rules that plain חרמים go to בדק הבית, like רב.

steps.title: Whose view allows redeeming for so little?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view lets property be redeemed onto coins worth less than it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of another detail in the story: the low price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The property was surely worth more than four זוזים. So the גמרא asks which Sage holds that redeeming for far less than the value works.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? According to whose view?

phrases.english: Like whom?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the four coins being worth much less than the property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the חרם question to the redemption price in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which Sage allows redeeming holy property for less than its value.

steps.title: Like שמואל: redeeming onto a פרוטה works
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה follows שמואל, who says holy property worth a מנה redeemed onto a פרוטה is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like שמואל, who said: Holy property worth a מנה that someone redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה follows שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that even a huge gap in value does not stop the redemption from working. So four זוזים are enough for the man's property.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy property belonging to the בית המקדש
A large sum, one hundred זוזים
The smallest coin value
Redeemed, no longer holy

phrases.english: Like Shmuel, who said:
Holy property worth a maneh
that one redeemed onto something worth a peruta is redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר: הֶקְדֵּשׁ שָׁוֶה מָנֶה שֶׁחִילְּלוֹ עַל שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה מְחוּלָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה follows שמואל, who says redemption for far less than the value works.

steps.title: Did שמואל allow it from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: שמואל only said it works after the fact, not that one may do it at the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say שמואל said this when someone already redeemed it. Did he say one may do it from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the link to שמואל. רב יהודה told the man to do it on purpose, but שמואל only spoke about something already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's word 'that one redeemed' describes a done deed: it works if it already happened. רב יהודה gave advice to do it from the start, which שמואל never clearly allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as a plan before acting
You can say, perhaps

phrases.english: Say that Shmuel said it where one already redeemed it,
did he say it from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל שֶׁחִילְּלוֹ, לְכַתְּחִלָּה מִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: Basing רב יהודה's advice on שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל only said it works after the fact, but רב יהודה told the man to do it from the start.

steps.title: Nowadays one may redeem onto less, even at the outset
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's rule that redeeming onto less works only after the fact applies only when the בית המקדש stands. Nowadays it is allowed even at the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: That limit applies only when the Temple stands, because then the Temple loses money. But nowadays one may do it even at the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 27. It says שמואל's limit (only after the fact) was only for the time of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming onto less is forbidden at the outset only because בדק הבית loses money. Today there is no בדק הבית to lose anything. So the reason for the limit is gone, and רב יהודה could tell the man to do it at the outset.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only (in a certain case)
A loss (here, a loss to the Temple treasury)
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
At the outset; doing it that way on purpose from the start

phrases.english: This matter applies only
phrases.notes: He means the limit from step 27: redeeming onto less is okay only after the fact, not planned from the start.

phrases.english: at a time when the Temple is standing
since there is a loss
but nowadays
even at the outset

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to a time period (only when the בית המקדש stands)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל allows redeeming onto less only after the fact, so רב יהודה could not tell the man to do it at the outset.
steps.terutzMaskana: The only reason for that limit is the loss to the Temple. Today there is no such loss, so it is allowed even at the outset.

steps.title: Then why not redeem onto just one פרוטה?
steps.stepSummary: If redeeming onto less is fine today, why did רב יהודה need four זוזים? A פרוטה should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even a פרוטה should be enough too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If any small amount works today, why did רב יהודה ask for four זוזים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said the Temple's loss does not matter nowadays. Then the amount should not matter either, and the smallest coin should do. Asking for four זוזים looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
The smallest coin that counts as having value

phrases.english: If so,
then even a פרוטה should work too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 28 by pointing to a detail of the story
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's choice of four זוזים, given the answer in step 28
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Temple's loss does not matter today, any amount works. So four זוזים is more than needed.

steps.title: Four זוזים were used to make the matter public
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asked for four זוזים so the redemption would be noticed and talked about.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was to publicize the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: a larger sum was used so people would know the property had been properly redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By law a פרוטה would work. But a noticeable sum makes the act known. Then people will understand why the man is now allowed to use the property.

keyTerms.meaning: To make the matter public, so people know about it

phrases.english: To publicize the matter

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, nowadays one may redeem חרם property onto less than its value even at the outset. Four זוזים were used only to make it public.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: A practical reason not required by law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four זוזים means a פרוטה would not have worked.
steps.terutzMaskana: A פרוטה would work by law. The larger sum was only to make the redemption known.

steps.title: עולא would have given everything to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: עולא says that if he had been there, he would have given all the property to the כהנים, not redeemed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: If I had been there, I would have given it all to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion enters. עולא disagrees with how רב יהודה handled the man's חרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה had the property redeemed and the coins thrown away. עולא says it should not be redeemed at all. All of it should go to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests, descendants of אהרן

phrases.english: עולא said: If I had been there
phrases.notes: He means at the case of the man who asked רב יהודה what to do (step 23).

phrases.english: I would have given all of it to the priests

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different ruling on the same story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man's חרם property should have been given entirely to the כהנים.

steps.title: So עולא holds plain חרמים go to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: From עולא's words, the גמרא concludes that he holds plain חרמים belong to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems עולא holds that plain חרמים go to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from עולא's words. This is the opposite of what it concluded about רב יהודה in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Property that goes to the כהנים cannot be redeemed. Only property for בדק הבית can be. So the two אמוראים disagree about the basic question: where does a סתם חרם go?

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems; this shows that
He holds (this view)
Plain חרמים, where the person did not say who they are for

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה: plain חרמים go to בדק הבית, so they can be redeemed. עולא: plain חרמים go to the כהנים, so they are given to them.

phrases.english: So it seems that עולא holds
plain dedications go to the priests

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the underlying view from עולא's statement in step 31
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא holds סתם חרמים go to the כהנים, unlike רב יהודה, who holds they go to בדק הבית.

steps.title: A ברייתא: some laws apply only when יובל is in force
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the idea that חרם laws apply today. It lists עבד עברי, שדה החרם and בתי ערי חומה as applying only when יובל is in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: עבד עברי applies only when יובל is in force, as it says, 'he shall serve with you until the year of יובל.' שדה החרם applies only when יובל is in force, as it says, 'and it shall go out in the יובל, and he shall return to his possession.' Houses of walled cities apply only when יובל is in force, as it says, 'it shall not go out in the יובל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against both רב יהודה and עולא, who both treated חרמים as real today. It is setting up the attack by quoting the ברייתא, and the punch comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions assumed that a חרם made nowadays takes effect. The ברייתא ties several laws to the time of יובל, including שדה החרם. Since there is no יובל today, it may follow that חרמים do not apply now either.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish servant who was sold
The Jubilee year, every 50th year
A field that was dedicated as חרם
Houses in walled cities, which have special sale laws
Is in force; applies

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The ברייתא is quoted to ask whether חרם laws, which רב יהודה and עולא just discussed, even apply when there is no יובל.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The law of a Hebrew servant does not apply
except at a time when the Jubilee is in force
as it says: “Until the year of Jubilee he shall serve with you”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:40

phrases.english: And the law of a dedicated field does not apply
except at a time when the Jubilee is in force
as it says: “And it shall go out in the Jubilee, and he shall return to his possession”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:28. This פסוק talks about a family field going back to its owner in the יובל.

phrases.english: The law of houses of walled cities does not apply
except at a time when the Jubilee is in force
as it says: “It shall not go out in the Jubilee”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:30

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared assumption of steps 23–32 that חרמים take effect nowadays
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption, shared by רב יהודה and עולא, that חרם laws apply today
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says laws tied to יובל, including שדה החרם, apply only when יובל is in force. With no יובל today, חרמים may not apply at all.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: dedicated fields apply only with the יובל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says the laws of שדה חרמים apply only when the יובל is in force, and brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: the laws of a dedicated field only apply when the יובל is in force. The פסוק says: 'And the field, when it goes out in the יובל, shall be holy to ה׳, like a dedicated field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from step 33. This line is what makes the challenge clear: חרם laws seem tied to the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the dedicated field together with the יובל, so רבי שמעון בן יוחי learns they go together. Since there is no יובל today, it seems חרם should not work today. That clashes with the story where רב יהודה treated a חרם as real.

keyTerms.meaning: A field dedicated by a חרם vow
The fiftieth year, when fields return to their owners
Is in force, applies

steps.confusionAlert: The question is about whether the חרם law applies today. It is not saying a חרם stops being a kind of הקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
The laws of a dedicated field do not apply
except at a time when the Jubilee is in force,
as it says: "And the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

phrases.english: shall be holy to ה׳, like a dedicated field."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: אֵין שְׂדֵה חֲרָמִין נוֹהֲגִין אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 33
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that חרם laws apply today (רב יהודה's ruling in פומבדיתא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שדה חרמים only apply with the יובל, and there is no יובל today, a חרם today should have no effect.

steps.title: גר תושב also applies only with the יובל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds that the laws of גר תושב apply only when the יובל is in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: the laws of a גר תושב only apply when the יובל is in force.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more opinion to its list of things tied to the יובל. The reason for it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the challenge about חרם. It is simply the rest of the ברייתא, which the גמרא quotes in full.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who lives in ארץ ישראל and keeps the seven מצוות of בני נח

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
The laws of a resident alien do not apply
except at a time when the Jubilee is in force.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אֵין גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נוֹהֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גר תושב laws apply only when the יובל is in force.

steps.title: רב ביבי explains the גר תושב rule with the word 'טוב'
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי gives the source: the word 'טוב' appears with עבד עברי and with גר תושב, so they share the יובל rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said: What is the reason? It is learned from 'טוב' and 'טוב'. Here, about the עבד עברי, it says 'because it is good for him with you.' There, about the גר תושב, it says 'where it is good for him, do not wrong him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי, an אמורא, explains why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר ties גר תושב to the יובל. With this the challenge from the ברייתא is fully set out, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד עברי can only be sold when the יובל is in force. Because the same word 'טוב' appears with both, the גר תושב gets the same rule. The ברייתא as a whole shows that חרם laws depend on the יובל, so the problem from step 33 is now complete.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
It is learned (by a גזירה שוה)
Good. This is the shared word that links the two פסוקים

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said: What is the reason?
It is learned from "good" and "good"
phrases.notes: The same word shows up in two פסוקים, so the rule from one is carried over to the other.

phrases.english: It is written here: "Because it is good for him with you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:16. This one is about an עבד עברי.

phrases.english: and it is written there: "Where it is good for him, do not wrong him"!
phrases.notes: דברים 23:17. This one is about a גר תושב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי: מַאי טַעְמָא? אַתְיָא ״טוֹב״ ״טוֹב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion in step 35
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is גר תושב tied to the יובל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the word 'טוב', which links it to עבד עברי, who exists only with the יובל.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about land, the פומבדיתא story was about movables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא talks about land, while רב יהודה's case dealt with movable things.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (the ברייתא) is about land. That (the story in פומבדיתא) is about movable things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 33-36 by splitting the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says שדה חרמים need the יובל, and a שדה is land. A חרם on movable things does not depend on the יובל, so it still works today. So רב יהודה was right to require a redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
Land, real estate
Movable property

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is with land,
that is with movable property.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the ברייתא and 'that' is the story with רב יהודה in פומבדיתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בִּמְקַרְקְעֵי, הָא בְּמִטַּלְטְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say no חרם works today.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a חרם on land needs the יובל. A חרם on movables works today.

steps.title: But the פומבדיתא story also involved land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the case in פומבדיתא included land too, and רב יהודה still required redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the story in פומבדיתא was also with land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 37.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the story included land, then the land-vs.-movables split does not explain why רב יהודה treated that חרם as real today.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here is a problem
Incident, story

phrases.english: But the incident of Pumbedita
was also with land!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא בִּמְקַרְקְעֵי נָמֵי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 37
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פומבדיתא case included land, yet the חרם was treated as working.

steps.title: Land outside ארץ ישראל counts like movables
steps.stepSummary: Land in חוצה לארץ is treated like movable property of ארץ ישראל, so a חרם on it still works today.
steps.simpleTranslation: Land outside ארץ ישראל is considered like movable property of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push-back and closes this topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יובל rules for fields only apply to land in ארץ ישראל. Land in פומבדיתא, which is in בבל, follows the rules for movables. So the חרם there worked even without a יובל, and רב יהודה's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside ארץ ישראל
Is like, is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: A חרם on land in ארץ ישראל needs the יובל. A חרם on movables, or on land outside ארץ ישראל, still works today.

phrases.english: Land outside the Land of Israel
is considered like movable property of Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקַרְקְעֵי דְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ כְּמִטַּלְטְלֵי דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 38
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category of the property
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The land in פומבדיתא should count as land that needs the יובל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Land outside ארץ ישראל is treated like movables, so the חרם works today.

steps.title: משנה: two פסוקים about making a בכור holy seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל points out that one פסוק says 'you shall make holy' a בכור and another says 'he shall not make it holy', and neither can simply be read alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: one פסוק says 'you shall make holy' and another says 'he shall not make holy'. You cannot say 'make holy', because it already says 'shall not make holy'. You cannot say 'shall not make holy', because it already says 'make holy'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי ישמעאל sets up a contradiction between two פסוקים about a בכור, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים talk about a firstborn animal. One seems to order us to make it holy, and the other seems to forbid it. Each פסוק blocks the simple reading of the other, so we need a way to make both true.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall make holy
He shall not make holy
It is impossible to say
A firstborn animal, which is holy from birth

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Rabbi Yishmael says:
One verse says "you shall consecrate,"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:19

phrases.english: and one verse says "he shall not consecrate."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:26

phrases.english: It is impossible to say "you shall consecrate"
since it is already stated "he shall not consecrate,"
and it is impossible to say "he shall not consecrate"
since it is already stated "you shall consecrate."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״תַּקְדִּישׁ״, וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״לֹא יַקְדִּישׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two פסוקים about making a בכור holy seem to contradict each other, and neither can be read alone. The answer follows.

steps.title: Resolving the two verses: value yes, altar no
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל settles the clash between the פסוקים. A בכור can be given as הקדש עילוי, but not as הקדש מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do the two פסוקים fit together? You may give the בכור to הקדש in the form of its value, but you may not make it holy as a different קרבן for the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל finishes his statement from the משנה. He shows how both פסוקים can be true at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 40 left a clash: one פסוק says 'make it holy' and another says 'do not make it holy.' Each פסוק covers a different kind of הקדש. Giving its value to הקדש is allowed, but turning a בכור into some other קרבן is not, because it already belongs to the altar as a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: How then? This phrase is used to bring two texts that seem to clash together.
A gift of value: you donate to הקדש the money worth of something you own
Making an animal holy as a קרבן for the altar
A firstborn male animal, which is holy and goes to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל does not say a בכור cannot be dedicated at all. One kind of dedication works (value) and the other kind does not (as a different קרבן).

phrases.english: How can these be reconciled?
You may consecrate it as a consecration of value,
phrases.notes: The owner gives הקדש the amount he would pay for the right to choose which כהן receives the בכור.

phrases.english: but you may not consecrate it as a consecration for the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 40
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק refers to a different kind of הקדש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to say opposite things about consecrating a בכור
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Make holy' covers הקדש עילוי; 'do not make holy' covers הקדש מזבח

steps.title: How the רבנן use the two פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not need these פסוקים for רבי ישמעאל's split. 'Do not make holy' teaches a לאו. 'You shall make holy' teaches a מצוה to declare a newborn בכור holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They need 'do not consecrate' for a prohibition. They need 'you shall consecrate' for what a ברייתא teaches: how do we know it is a מצוה to declare a בכור born in your flock holy? Because it says, 'the male you shall consecrate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה. It asks what the רבנן, who disagree with רבי ישמעאל, do with the same two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל used the pair of פסוקים to split value from altar. The רבנן give each פסוק its own separate job. 'Do not make holy' becomes a real לאו against using a בכור as another קרבן. 'You shall make holy' becomes a positive מצוה to declare the newborn בכור holy out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for: this פסוק is used to teach something else
A Torah prohibition, a negative commandment
It is a מצוה to declare it holy out loud
Flock, herd

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the practical idea comes from that a person should say out loud that a newborn בכור is holy, even though it is holy anyway.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And the Rabbis (what do they do with these verses)?
'Shall not consecrate' is needed for a prohibition,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:26

phrases.english: 'You shall consecrate' is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know, about a firstborn born in one's flock,
that it is a מצוה to consecrate it?
As it is stated: 'The male you shall consecrate.'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the opposing view handles the verses רבי ישמעאל used in step 41
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the רבנן learn from the two פסוקים, since they do not use them like רבי ישמעאל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One פסוק teaches a לאו, and the other teaches a מצוה to declare a בכור holy

steps.title: Why רבי ישמעאל sees no מצוה to declare it holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל does not learn a מצוה to declare a בכור holy, because it is holy from birth no matter what.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? If the owner doesn't declare it holy, is it not holy? Its holiness comes from the womb. Since it is holy even when he doesn't declare it, there is no need to declare it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי ישמעאל does not agree with the רבנן's reading. In his view, saying the בכור is holy adds nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unspoken question is why רבי ישמעאל doesn't learn the מצוה from 'you shall make holy.' His answer is that a בכור becomes holy automatically at birth. A מצוה to make holy something that is already fully holy makes no sense to him, so he uses the פסוק for הקדש עילוי instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Its holiness comes from the womb: it is holy automatically at birth
To declare it holy

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a בכור is holy from birth. The רבנן still see a מצוה to say so out loud. רבי ישמעאל says there is no need, so he uses the פסוק for הקדש עילוי.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael (why doesn't he learn this מצוה)?

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵיהּ, לָא קָדֵישׁ?
phrases.english: If one does not consecrate it, is it not consecrated?
Its sanctity is from the womb,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּכִי לָא מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵיהּ קָדוֹשׁ,
phrases.english: and since even when one does not consecrate it, it is holy,
he does not need to consecrate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי ישמעאל against the reading of the רבנן in step 42
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical rejection of the other reading: the מצוה would be pointless
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'You shall make holy' should teach a מצוה to declare the בכור holy, as the רבנן say
steps.terutzMaskana: A בכור is holy from birth, so there is no need to declare it, and the פסוק is free to teach הקדש עילוי

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המקדיש שדהו
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the chapter המקדיש שדהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק המקדיש שדהו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line that ends a chapter of the גמרא. The discussion of פרק המקדיש שדהו is now finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the chapter and expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a chapter
'One who consecrates his field': the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you,
'One Who Consecrates His Field.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after the final discussion
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter המקדיש שדהו is complete.
